column1: # The migration files a DEPLOYED database has already journalled.
# One row per file, `<filename>\t<sha256 of the file's bytes>`, sorted by
# on the production cluster. Refresh it with:
# WHY THE CHECKSUMS COME FROM THE JOURNAL AND NOT FROM THE TREE. The migrate
# runner hashes each file's source bytes and refuses every later run against a
# database whose journal recorded a different hash, permanently, with no
# self-healing arm. Editing an applied file therefore bricks that database; it
# blocked a production roll for a full day on 2026-08-19. A checksum recomputed
# from the tree would be updated BY the edit and would endorse exactly the
# change this file exists to refuse, so these values may only ever be copied
# from a database that recorded them.
# A file BELOW the last row here is not yet deployed anywhere and is free to be
# edited. The gate that reads this file
# rows are a PREFIX of db/migrations-ts in filename order, which is the order
# the runner applies in, so "released" and "the oldest N files" are the same
